[Finite truncations] Put $\Psi_{N}:=\sum_{r\in J_{N}}s_{r}\kappa(v_{r}\otimes u_{r})$ for an increasing sequence of finite subsets $J_{N}\uparrow J$. For bounded $X\in\mathcal B(H)$ and $N$ one has, using the tensor identity of [F1] on elementary tensors, $\langle(X\otimes I_{K})\Psi_{N},\Psi_{N}\rangle=\sum_{r,r'\in J_{N}}s_{r}s_{r'}\langle Xv_{r},v_{r'}\rangle\langle u_{r},u_{r'}\rangle=\sum_{r\in J_{N}}s_{r}^{2}\langle Xv_{r},v_{r}\rangle$ by orthonormality of $(u_{r})$; since $\Psi_{N}\to\Psi$, $\|X\otimes I_{K}\|\le\|X\|$ and $\sum_{r}s_{r}^{2}<\infty$, the sesquilinear form is continuous and the series converges absolutely, so $\operatorname{tr}(\rho(X\otimes I_{K}))=\langle(X\otimes I_{K})\Psi,\Psi\rangle=\sum_{r}s_{r}^{2}\langle Xv_{r},v_{r}\rangle$.

[Reduction identity] Let $S:=\sum_{r}s_{r}^{2}T_{v_{r},v_{r}}$, a trace-class operator with $S\ge0$ and $\operatorname{tr}S=1$ by [F3] and absolute convergence. For bounded $X$, step 1.2 and [F2] give $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A}X)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho(X\otimes I_{K}))=\sum_{r}s_{r}^{2}\langle Xv_{r},v_{r}\rangle$; taking $X=T_{w,w'}$ and using [F3] twice, $\langle\rho_{A}w,w'\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{A}T_{w,w'})=\sum_{r}s_{r}^{2}\langle T_{w,w'}v_{r},v_{r}\rangle=\sum_{r}s_{r}^{2}\langle v_{r},w'\rangle\langle w,v_{r}\rangle=\langle Sw,w'\rangle$ for all $w,w'\in H$, so $\rho_{A}=S$ by taking $w'=(\rho_{A}-S)w$ and using $\|(\rho_{A}-S)w\|^{2}=0$; interchanging the factors gives $\rho_{B}=\sum_{r}s_{r}^{2}T_{u_{r},u_{r}}$ with the same argument.

[Purity and product criterion] By [F1] and step 2.1, $\operatorname{tr}\rho_{A}^{2}=\sum_{r}s_{r}^{4}=\operatorname{tr}\rho_{B}^{2}$ and $\operatorname{tr}\rho_{A}^{2}=1$ holds exactly when exactly one $s_{r}$ is nonzero and exactly when $\Psi$ is a product vector; purity of $\rho_{A}$ is equivalent to $\operatorname{tr}\rho_{A}^{2}=1$ by [F4], and likewise for $\rho_{B}$. If exactly one $s_{r_{0}}$ is nonzero, then $s_{r_{0}}^{2}=1$ and $\Psi=\kappa(v_{r_{0}}\otimes u_{r_{0}})$ is a product vector, so $\rho=\rho_{A}\otimes\rho_{B}$ by [F5]; conversely for a product vector [F5] gives $\rho_{A}=T_{u,u}$, $\rho_{B}=T_{v,v}$, which are pure by [F3] and [F4]. Thus every positive $s_r^2$ equals its square and is one; their sum one forces exactly one coefficient. Finally [F6] identifies this product case exactly with separability, proving (vi); in the non-product case it gives entanglement and the stated strict trace-norm witness.

Adopt the framework's composition, state and measurement readings for the
internal factors of two declared spin-half particles
([[thm-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-tensor-spin-composition]],
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-composite-systems-and-local-readouts]],
[[def-nrqm-composites-framework-reduced-preparations]],
[[def-nrqm-measurement-framework-declared-measurements-and-instruments]]),
and assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$V=\mathbb C^{2}$ be a declared spin-half internal factor with orthonormal
basis $(e_{+},e_{-})$ and spin matrices $J_{i}=\tfrac12\sigma_{i}$ of
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]], so that
$S_{i}:=\hbar J_{i}$ and, for a unit vector $n\in\mathbb R^{3}$,
$S_{n}:=\sum_{i}n_{i}S_{i}$; let the declared composite of the two internal
factors be $V\widehat\otimes V$ with the local spin observables
$S_{n}\otimes I$ and $I\otimes S_{m}$, read as bounded assigned sharp
observables of the two factors with unit $\mathrm{J\,s}$
([[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]] clause
(c), [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). Put
$$\Psi:=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\bigl(\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{-})-\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{+})\bigr),\qquad \rho:=T_{\Psi,\Psi}\in D(V\widehat\otimes V),$$
the **singlet preparation**, and let $\rho_{A}=\operatorname{Tr}_{B}\rho$,
$\rho_{B}=\operatorname{Tr}_{A}\rho$ be its reduced preparations. Then:
 
**(a) Singlet data.** $\Psi$ is a unit vector; $S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i}\Psi=0$ for
all $i$; $\rho_{A}=\rho_{B}=\tfrac12 I$; and the Schmidt expansion of $\Psi$
is $\Psi=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\bigl(\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{-})-\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{+})\bigr)$
with two equal coefficients, so $\Psi$ is not a product vector and both
reduced preparations are mixed with $\operatorname{tr}\rho_{A}^{2}=\tfrac12$.
 
**(b) Joint directional laws.** For unit vectors $a,b\in\mathbb R^{3}$ with
$\cos\theta=a\cdot b$ and for the two-outcome local measurements
$(P_{a,\pm},P_{a,\mp})$ and $(P_{b,\pm},P_{b,\mp})$ of the observables
$S_{a}\otimes I$ and $I\otimes S_{b}$, the joint probabilities are
$$p(+,+)=p(-,-)=\tfrac12\sin^{2}\tfrac{\theta}{2},\qquad p(+,-)=p(-,+)=\tfrac12\cos^{2}\tfrac{\theta}{2},$$
where the first sign refers to the outcome $+\hbar/2$ or $-\hbar/2$ of
$S_{a}\otimes I$ and the second to that of $I\otimes S_{b}$;
in particular the four numbers are nonnegative and sum to one.
 
**(c) Correlation function.** With the product $\sigma\tau$ of the two sign
labels,
$$\mathbb E(a,b):=\sum_{\sigma,\tau\in\{\pm\}}\sigma\tau\,p(\sigma,\tau) =-\cos\theta=-a\cdot b .$$
In particular $\mathbb E(a,a)=-1$ and $\mathbb E(a,-a)=+1$: the outcomes are
perfectly anti-correlated for equal directions.

$p_{A}(\pm)=\tfrac12$ and $p_{B}(\pm)=\tfrac12$, independent of $b$ and of
$a$ respectively; the reduced preparations $\rho_{A}=\rho_{B}=\tfrac12 I$ are
unchanged by performing the local measurement on the other factor and
discarding its record, in agreement with
[[pthm-nrqm-composites-local-instruments-and-no-signalling]] clause (b).
 
**(e) Scope.** This is a thought experiment of the declared framework: the
composite is an internal-factor composite, the particles are not assigned
spatial positions or worldlines here, and no spatial separation, temporal
order, relativistic consideration, measurement or recorded data enters. The
computation asserts no empirical correlation and draws no conclusion about
nature; in particular it makes no claim about the completeness of the
framework or about any hidden-variable model.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,K$ be
nonzero complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let
$H\widehat\otimes K$ be their completed tensor product with inclusion $\kappa$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]). Density operators are
the self-adjoint positive trace-class operators of trace one
([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a),
[[def-trace-class-operator]]), and for $u,u'\in H$, $v,v'\in K$ the rank-one
operator $T_{u\otimes v,\,u'\otimes v'}$ is the one of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]].

**(a) Product vectors and pure product states.** A vector $\Psi\in
H\widehat\otimes K$ is a **product vector** when $\Psi=\kappa(u\otimes v)$ for
some $u\in H$, $v\in K$. A **pure product state** of the composite is a
density operator of the form
$$T_{\Psi,\Psi},\qquad \Psi=\kappa(u\otimes v),\quad \|u\|=\|v\|=1 .$$
A vector is **non-product** when it is not a product vector.

**(b) Separable states.** Write $\mathcal P$ for the set of all pure product
states, a subset of the set $D(H\widehat\otimes K)$ of density operators. The
**separable states** are the elements of the trace-norm closed convex hull
$$\mathcal S(H,K):=\overline{\operatorname{conv}}\,\mathcal P \ \subseteq\ D(H\widehat\otimes K),$$
where $\operatorname{conv}$ denotes the set of finite convex combinations and
the closure is taken in the trace norm $\|\cdot\|_{1}$ of
[[thm-trace-class-is-a-two-sided-banach-operator-ideal]]. A state
$\rho\in D(H\widehat\otimes K)$ is **entangled** (with respect to the
declared splitting $H,K$) when $\rho\notin\mathcal S(H,K)$.

**(c) Conventions and elementary consequences of the form of the definition.**
The set $\operatorname{conv}\mathcal P$ consists exactly of the finite sums
$\sum_{j=1}^{n}w_{j}T_{\Psi_{j},\Psi_{j}}$ with $n\ge1$, weights $w_{j}\ge0$,
$\sum_{j}w_{j}=1$ and unit product vectors $\Psi_{j}$: such sums are convex
combinations of density operators and hence density operators
([[lem-nrqm-state-geometry-density-set-convex-and-complete]] clause (a);
the finite-dimensional case of that clause is the
[[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] expansion
applied to orthogonal pure states).
Every element of $\operatorname{conv}\mathcal P$ is a density operator, and
$\mathcal S(H,K)$ is a convex subset of $D(H\widehat\otimes K)$: if $\rho,\sigma$
are limits of convex combinations $\rho_{n}\to\rho$, $\sigma_{n}\to\sigma$ and
$t\in[0,1]$, then $t\rho+(1-t)\sigma$ is the trace-norm limit of the convex
combinations $t\rho_{n}+(1-t)\sigma_{n}$. Separability of a state is a
property of the declared splitting $(H,K)$; no assertion is made here about
its behaviour under a different factorization of a larger space.

**(d) Finite dimension.** When $H$ and $K$ are finite dimensional,
$\mathcal P$ is compact and $\operatorname{conv}\mathcal P$ is already closed
in the trace norm (it is a compact, hence closed, convex set in the
finite-dimensional space of endomorphisms of $H\widehat\otimes K$), so
$\mathcal S(H,K)=\operatorname{conv}\mathcal P$ and no closure convention is
needed. In the general case the closure in clause (b) is declared explicitly
and is part of the definition.

**(e) Pure-state specialization and status.** A pure state $T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ with $\|\Psi\|=1$ is separable in the precise trace-norm closed-convex-hull sense of clause (b) exactly when $\Psi$ is a product vector of clause (a); otherwise it is entangled. This is the proved mathematical specialization of [[lem-nrqm-composites-pure-state-separability-criterion]], whose locally defined $\mathcal P,\mathcal S$ are exactly those above. Clauses (a)-(e) fix mathematical vocabulary and adopt no physical assumption, dynamics, measurement or probability law. Whether a laboratory preparation realizes a separable or entangled state for the declared splitting remains a tested identification with uncertainty, not a consequence about nature of this definition.

If $(u_n)_{n\in J}$ is a finite or countable orthonormal family, with $J$ a finite initial segment of the positive integers or all positive integers, and $w_n\ge0$ with $\sum_nw_n=1$, then the sum $\rho:=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ converges in trace norm to a density operator with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=\sum_nw_n=1$. Conversely every density operator $\rho$ admits such an expansion whose weights are its positive eigenvalues counted with multiplicity and whose vectors are orthonormal eigenvectors; distinct expansions of the same $\rho$ exist when a positive eigenspace has dimension at least two.

derivations.claim: [Marginals] By [L2], $\operatorname{Tr}_{B}T_{e_{+}\otimes e_{-},e_{+}\otimes e_{-}}=T_{e_{+},e_{+}}$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_{B}T_{e_{-}\otimes e_{+},e_{-}\otimes e_{+}}=T_{e_{-},e_{-}}$, so the linearity of the partial trace gives $\operatorname{Tr}_{B}M=\frac12T_{e_{+},e_{+}}+\frac12T_{e_{-},e_{-}}=\frac12I$; likewise $\operatorname{Tr}_{A}M=\frac12I$. Together with $\rho_{A}=\frac12I$ from [L1] and $\rho_{\mathrm{proper}}=\frac12I$ by definition this is (i).

[Correlations of the product mixture] By [L2] and [L4] the joint outcome law of the local measurements of $S_{a}\otimes I$ and $I\otimes S_{b}$ in $M$ is the weighted average of the two product laws, so $\mathbb E_{M}(a,b)=\frac12\langle(a\cdot\sigma)e_{+},e_{+}\rangle\langle(b\cdot\sigma)e_{-},e_{-}\rangle+\frac12\langle(a\cdot\sigma)e_{-},e_{-}\rangle\langle(b\cdot\sigma)e_{+},e_{+}\rangle=\frac12(a_{3})(-b_{3})+\frac12(-a_{3})(b_{3})=-a_{3}b_{3}$; with [L1] this is (ii).

[Local indistinguishability and separability] Let $\tau_B$ be any preparation of $B$. Its density expansion is $\tau_B=\sum_jq_jT_{z_j,z_j}$ in trace norm, with unit $z_j$, $q_j>0$ and $\sum_jq_j=1$, by [L5]. The independent extension of the proper mixture is the trace-norm sum $\Omega=\sum_j(q_j/2)(T_{e_+\otimes z_j,e_+\otimes z_j}+T_{e_-\otimes z_j,e_-\otimes z_j})$: every summand is positive, and its trace norm equals its nonnegative trace, so the series converges with trace one by [L4], [L5]. The rank-one reduction formula [L2] and trace-norm continuity [L5] give $\operatorname{Tr}_B\Omega=(T_{e_+,e_+}+T_{e_-,e_-})/2=I_A/2$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_A\Omega=\tau_B$, which need not equal $I_B/2$. Since $\rho$ and $M$ also have reduction $I_A/2$ by [L1] and step 1.1, [L3] proves all local-$A$ readout laws agree for $\rho$, $M$ and this arbitrary-$B$ extension. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and let $H,K$ be nonzero complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]]) with $H\widehat\otimes K$ their completed tensor product ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]). Then for every $\Psi\in H\widehat\otimes K$ there are an at most countable index set $J$, orthonormal families $(v_r)_{r\in J}\subseteq H$ and $(u_r)_{r\in J}\subseteq K$, and numbers $s_r>0$ with

$$\Psi=\sum_{r\in J}s_r\,v_r\otimes u_r\qquad\text{(norm convergence in }H\widehat\otimes K),$$

and $\|\Psi\|^2=\sum_rs_r^2$. The $s_r$ are the positive square roots of the nonzero eigenvalues of $CC^*$, where $C:\overline{K_0}\to H_0$ is the linear coefficient operator on countable closed factor supports of $\Psi$, defined below; if $J$ is infinite then $s_r\to0$. For $\|\Psi\|=1$ the reduced density $\rho=\operatorname{Tr}_KT_{\Psi,\Psi}$ has $\operatorname{tr}\rho^2=\sum_rs_r^4$, and $\operatorname{tr}\rho^2=1$ holds exactly when exactly one $s_r$ is nonzero, i.e. exactly when $\Psi$ is a product vector. Mixed-state separability is a different, explicitly defined property and is not decided here.

For clarity, choose finite algebraic tensors converging to $\Psi$ and let $H_0\subseteq H$, $K_0\subseteq K$ be the closed spans of their factor vectors. These supports have finite/countable orthonormal bases, and $\Psi\in H_0\widehat\otimes K_0$. The conjugate Hilbert space $\overline{K_0}$ consists of symbols $\bar z$, with $a\bar z:=\overline{\bar a z}$ and $\langle\bar z,\bar w\rangle_{\overline{K_0}}:=\langle w,z\rangle_{K_0}$. For an orthonormal basis $(f_j)$ of $K_0$, write $\Psi=\sum_jh_j\otimes f_j$ and set $C\bar f_j=h_j$, extending linearly and continuously. The positive singular values and the nonzero spectrum of $CC^*$ are independent of these supports and bases, as the reduced-state identity proved below shows.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$, $K$
and $L$ be real or complex Hilbert spaces ([[def-hilbert-space]]). Then:

1. the trace-class operators $\mathcal S_1(H,K)$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]])
   form a linear subspace of $\mathcal B(H,K)$ on which $\|\cdot\|_1$ is a norm,
   and
   $$\|T\|\le\|T\|_1\qquad\text{for every }T\in\mathcal S_1(H,K)$$
   ([[def-operator-norm]]);
2. if $T\in\mathcal S_1(H,K)$ and $A\in\mathcal B(K,L)$, $B\in\mathcal B(H_0,H)$
   are bounded linear operators on Hilbert spaces $H_0,L$, then
   $ATB\in\mathcal S_1(H_0,L)$ and
   $$\|ATB\|_1\le\|A\|\,\|T\|_1\,\|B\| ;$$
3. $(\mathcal S_1(H,K),\|\cdot\|_1)$ is a Banach space: every
   $\|\cdot\|_1$-Cauchy sequence in $\mathcal S_1(H,K)$ has a limit in
   $\mathcal S_1(H,K)$ to which it converges in $\|\cdot\|_1$
   ([[def-banach-space]], [[def-norm-and-normed-space]],

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
real or complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]) and let
$T\in\mathcal B(H)$ be trace class ([[def-trace-class-operator]]). Then:

1. for every **nuclear representation** $Tx=\sum_j\langle x,u_j\rangle v_j$ of
   $T$ (operator-norm convergence of the partial sums,
   $\sum_j\|u_j\|\|v_j\|<+\infty$), the scalar series $\sum_j\langle v_j,u_j\rangle$
   converges absolutely and
   $$\Bigl|\sum_j\langle v_j,u_j\rangle\Bigr|\le\sum_j\|u_j\|\,\|v_j\| ;$$
2. the sum $\sum_j\langle v_j,u_j\rangle$ depends only on $T$; denoting it
   $\operatorname{tr}(T)$, one has

   for **every** nuclear representation of $T$. This defines $\operatorname{tr}(T)$

3. for every supplied Hilbert basis $E$ of $H$,
   $\operatorname{tr}_E(T)=\operatorname{tr}(T)$
   ([[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]]);
4. the trace is linear in the trace-class variable and bounded by the trace

derivations.claim: [Maximum and the strict gap] By [F2], $\lambda_r>0$ and $\sum_r\lambda_r=1$. Fix one $r_0\in J$ and put $c=\lambda_{r_0}>0$. The set $E=\{r:\lambda_r\ge c\}$ is nonempty and finite: any finite subset of $E$ with $N$ elements has weight sum at least $Nc\le1$, so $E$ has at most $\lfloor1/c\rfloor$ elements. The maximum $m$ on this finite set is a maximum on $J$, since every weight outside $E$ is below $c\le m$. If $\Psi$ is non-product, [F2] gives at least two positive weights; at an index $r_*$ attaining $m$, another positive weight implies $m<\sum_r\lambda_r=1$.

[Finite orthogonal estimates] For an orthonormal family $(e_r)$, a vector $x$ and a finite set $F$, expanding $\|x-\sum_{r\in F}\langle x,e_r\rangle e_r\|^2$ gives $\|x\|^2-\sum_{r\in F}|\langle x,e_r\rangle|^2\ge0$. Thus for unit $a,b$ the sums of $|\langle v_r,a\rangle|^2$ and $|\langle u_r,b\rangle|^2$ are each at most one, using conjugate symmetry and the supremum of finite sums. For finite complex sequences $(\alpha_r),(\beta_r)$, Cauchy–Schwarz gives $|\sum_r\alpha_r\beta_r|\le(\sum_r|\alpha_r|^2)^{1/2}(\sum_r|\beta_r|^2)^{1/2}$: this follows by expanding $\sum_r|\alpha_r-t\overline{\beta_r}|^2\ge0$ with $t=(\sum_r\alpha_r\beta_r)/(\sum_r|\beta_r|^2)$ when the denominator is positive, and is immediate otherwise.

[Exact continuity of the fixed trace witness] For every trace-class $T$ on $L$, [F3] gives $\operatorname{tr}(TP_\Psi)=\langle T\Psi,\Psi\rangle$ and $|\operatorname{tr}(TP_\Psi)|\le\|T\Psi\|\|\Psi\|\le\|T\|\le\|T\|_1$, since $\|\Psi\|=1$. Applying this estimate to $T-S$ proves $|\operatorname{tr}(TP_\Psi)-\operatorname{tr}(SP_\Psi)|\le\|T-S\|_1$. Thus this particular bounded trace functional is 1-Lipschitz; no unspecified continuity theorem or unbounded cyclicity is used. Also $P_\Psi\Psi=\Psi$, so $\operatorname{tr}(P_\Psi^2)=\langle P_\Psi\Psi,\Psi\rangle=1$.

[The overlap bound, with the conjugations fixed] For a finite Schmidt truncation $\Psi_F$, [F1] gives $\langle\Psi_F,\kappa(a\otimes b)\rangle=\sum_{r\in F}s_r\langle v_r,a\rangle\langle u_r,b\rangle$; equivalently it is the conjugate of $\sum_{r\in F}s_r\langle a,v_r\rangle\langle b,u_r\rangle$. Applying step 1.2 to $\alpha_r=s_r\langle v_r,a\rangle$ and $\beta_r=\langle u_r,b\rangle$ gives a modulus bound $(\sum_{r\in F}\lambda_r|\langle v_r,a\rangle|^2)^{1/2}(\sum_{r\in F}|\langle u_r,b\rangle|^2)^{1/2}\le\sqrt m$. The Schmidt truncations converge in norm [F2], so continuity of the Hilbert pairing passes this bound to $\Psi$. At $a=v_{r_*}$ and $b=u_{r_*}$, orthonormality gives overlap $s_{r_*}$ and squared overlap $m$.

[Convex hull and its closure] For unit product $q=\kappa(a\otimes b)$, [F3] and first-linear conjugate symmetry give $\operatorname{tr}(T_{q,q}P_\Psi)=\langle T_{q,q}\Psi,\Psi\rangle=\langle\Psi,q\rangle\langle q,\Psi\rangle=|\langle\Psi,q\rangle|^2\le m$ by step 2.1. Trace linearity gives the same real bound for finite convex combinations. For $\sigma\in\mathcal S$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, the definition of closure supplies a single $\tau\in\operatorname{conv}\mathcal P$ with $\|\sigma-\tau\|_1<\varepsilon$. Step 1.3 gives $|\operatorname{tr}(\sigma P_\Psi)-\operatorname{tr}(\tau P_\Psi)|<\varepsilon$; letting $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ shows that $\operatorname{tr}(\sigma P_\Psi)$ is real and at most $m$. This neighborhood argument does not select a sequence of approximants.

[Equivalence and distance] If $\Psi$ is non-product, steps 1.1, 1.3 and 3.1 give $\operatorname{tr}(P_\Psi^2)=1>m\ge\operatorname{tr}(\sigma P_\Psi)$ for all $\sigma\in\mathcal S$, so $P_\Psi\notin\mathcal S$. Moreover step 1.3 gives $\|P_\Psi-\sigma\|_1\ge|\operatorname{tr}((P_\Psi-\sigma)P_\Psi)|=1-\operatorname{tr}(\sigma P_\Psi)\ge1-m$. Conversely a unit product vector has $P_\Psi\in\mathcal P\subseteq\mathcal S$. If initially $\Psi=\kappa(x\otimes y)$ with arbitrary nonzero factors, [F1] gives $\|x\|\|y\|=1$; therefore $a=x/\|x\|$ and $b=\|x\|y$ are unit and $\Psi=\kappa(a\otimes b)$. This proves the full claimed equivalence for the declared trace-norm closure and the strict witness bound.
